body:
OK, so I think this approach works, but it's very confusing right now because it makes it look like we define a distinct agent for each Window.

Maybe a way to phrase this is to flip it and define five classes of agents (one for each type of global), and then say something about how e.g. each URSOBC creates a single Window-agent. (As does each WorkerGlobalScope, WorkletGlobalScope, etc.) You can then add a note about how with these definitions, every Realm belongs to an agent.

---

Upon re-reading the spec I see I had previously misread and thought it said that each URSOBC got its own event loop. I think that may still be necessary with the stuff SAB makes observable, but I am not sure, and we don't need to block on redefining event loop, since this approach appears good. I will file a separate issue to check on that.
This all looks pretty good to me, hope my comments don't retread too much ground already discussed, as I didn't read all the background.

My biggest problem here is that I don't quite see how this interacts with the requirements around agents and agent clusters in the ES spec.

Say I have a page loaded in a tab.  It does a window.open to a similar-origin page.  That similar-origin page starts a dedicated worker.  That worker starts a child worker.  Then I navigate the opened thing, which terminates both workers.

Per ES spec, there must be "reliable APIs" that allow all this to "coordinate" such that the original page knows the inner worker got terminated, and can identify the thing (the inner worker) that got terminated.

Is the idea that the combination of window.opener and postMessage and unload event is enough to constitute a "reliable API" here?  Writing something on top of this that actually reliably and non-racily communicates back to the opener page the precise state of the workers on the opened page just before termination doesn't seem trivial to me...
LGTM, let's merge this (and probably the tests too).
